title: A New Chapter of the Coronavirus

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访内容，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, the United States takes a step backward in the pandemic, warning that even vaccinated Americans may spread the virus,
sentences.zh: 今天，美国在疫情应对上倒退了一步，官方警告称即使是接种过疫苗的美国人也可能传播病毒，

sentences.en: and asking millions of them to resume wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 并要求数百万民众重新开始佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Apoorva Mondavili, about this new chapter of the virus.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事阿普尔瓦·曼达维利谈论了关于这种病毒的新篇章。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月2日，星期一。

sentences.en: Hey, Apoorva.
sentences.zh: 嘿，阿普尔瓦。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: My sense is that you do not come bearing good news.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是你这次带来的不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: I do not.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: Well, I have only come to expect that from you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我对你一向只抱有这种预期。

sentences.en: Could be worse, though.
sentences.zh: 不过情况可能会更糟。

sentences.en: Could be worse.
sentences.zh: 可能会更糟。

sentences.en: Could it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: So, as I think we're hinting at, a lot has changed since we spoke to you exactly one week ago.
sentences.zh: 那么，正如我们刚才暗示的那样，自我们一周前与你交谈以来，发生了很多变化。

sentences.en: And that conversation was about breakthrough infections of COVID-19, vaccinated people getting the virus because of the Delta variant.
sentences.zh: 那次谈话是关于新冠肺炎的突破性感染，即接种过疫苗的人因为德尔塔变异株而感染病毒。

sentences.en: And right after we spoke,
sentences.zh: 就在我们谈话之后，

sentences.en: we got a bunch of new information about those kind of infections that really began to change how the government and a lot of other people are approaching the entire pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一系列关于此类感染的新信息，这些信息真正开始改变政府和许多其他人应对整个疫情的方式。

sentences.en: So, talk us through all of that.
sentences.zh: 那么，请为我们梳理一下这些情况。

sentences.en: So, last time when we talked, we were talking mainly about anecdotal cases of vaccinated people getting infected, these breakthrough infections.
sentences.zh: 上次我们交谈时，主要讨论的是接种疫苗者被感染的零星病例，也就是这些突破性感染。

sentences.en: I was describing these incidents of breakthrough infections in weddings and family gatherings.
sentences.zh: 我当时描述了在婚礼和家庭聚会中发生的这些突破性感染事件。

sentences.en: And there was this one outbreak in Provincetown, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 当时在马萨诸塞州的普罗温斯敦发生了一次疫情爆发。

sentences.en: What changed this week is that the CDC looked into that Provincetown outbreak more closely.
sentences.zh: 本周的变化是，美国疾控中心（CDC）更仔细地调查了普罗温斯敦的那次疫情。

sentences.en: That outbreak has spread to now 900 people across the country.
sentences.zh: 那次疫情现在已经蔓延到全国900人。

sentences.en: About 450 of them are in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 其中约450人在马萨诸塞州。

sentences.en: And what the CDC and the Massachusetts Department of Health found is that not only can vaccinated people get infected,
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心和马萨诸塞州卫生部发现，接种过疫苗的人不仅会感染，

sentences.en: but they have about the same amount of virus in their nose and throat as unvaccinated people do.
sentences.zh: 而且他们鼻腔和喉咙里的病毒量与未接种疫苗的人大致相同。

sentences.en: And that's completely unexpected.
sentences.zh: 这完全出乎意料。

sentences.en: And why is that so important to our understanding of the virus?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对我们理解这种病毒如此重要？

sentences.en: If you have virus in your nose and throat, you can spread it.
sentences.zh: 如果你的鼻腔和喉咙里有病毒，你就能传播它。

sentences.en: And we did not expect that once somebody was vaccinated, that they would be very likely to get infected or to spread the virus to anybody else.
sentences.zh: 我们原本没料到，一旦有人接种了疫苗，他们还会很有可能被感染，或者把病毒传播给其他人。

sentences.en: What we learned this week is that if somebody who's vaccinated does get a breakthrough infection, they end up having a lot of virus in their nose and throat.
sentences.zh: 我们本周了解到的是，如果接种过疫苗的人确实发生了突破性感染，他们的鼻腔和喉咙里最终会有大量病毒。

sentences.en: And now they can spread that virus to people around them.
sentences.zh: 现在他们可以将病毒传播给周围的人。

sentences.en: So this new understanding is that a vaccinated person could potentially spread the virus just as much as an unvaccinated person who becomes infected.
sentences.zh: 所以，新的认识是，接种过疫苗的人传播病毒的可能性可能与被感染的未接种疫苗者一样大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We don't know how often a vaccinated person is likely to get infected.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道接种疫苗的人被感染的频率有多高。

sentences.en: It's looking like it's actually very rare.
sentences.zh: 看起来这实际上非常罕见。

sentences.en: But when that happens, when a vaccinated person does get infected, they end up with just as much virus in their nose and throat as an unvaccinated person.
sentences.zh: 但当这种情况发生时，当接种过疫苗的人确实被感染时，他们的鼻腔和喉咙里的病毒量最终会和未接种疫苗的人一样多。

sentences.en: And they may be just as likely to spread it to other people.
sentences.zh: 而且他们传播给其他人的可能性可能也一样大。

sentences.en: So just to be super clear, in order to have a breakthrough infection that could then lead to transmission in a vaccinated person, that person has to be infected by COVID.
sentences.zh: 为了非常明确一点，接种疫苗的人要发生可能导致传播的突破性感染，那个人必须先感染新冠病毒。

sentences.en: They can't just breathe it in the air from somebody and pass it on to somebody else without being infected.
sentences.zh: 他们不可能只是从别人那里吸入空气，然后在没有被感染的情况下就把病毒传给别人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And not only do you have to be infected, but you have to be infected and have enough virus in your nose,
sentences.zh: 不仅必须被感染，而且必须是感染后鼻腔里有足够的病毒，

sentences.en: have had enough opportunity for the virus to grow into these large amounts that you can then infect somebody else.
sentences.zh: 并且有足够的机会让病毒生长到足以感染他人的大量水平。

sentences.en: That's why it's as rare as it is.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这种情况如此罕见。

sentences.en: Okay, so now I want to understand the mechanics of this transmission.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在我想了解这种传播的机制。

sentences.en: What is happening inside a vaccinated person's nose that's allowing this transmission to happen?
sentences.zh: 接种过疫苗的人的鼻腔里发生了什么，导致了这种传播？

sentences.en: Because we had been told in the past that the vaccine was going to prevent the transmission of the virus.
sentences.zh: 因为我们过去被告知疫苗可以预防病毒的传播。

sentences.en: But what you're describing is the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但你所描述的却是相反的情况。

sentences.en: So this is a little bit complicated.
sentences.zh: 这有点复杂。

sentences.en: You know that the vaccines that we have are injected into the muscle.
sentences.zh: 你知道我们现有的疫苗是注射到肌肉里的。

sentences.en: And from there, the vaccines do a really good job of stimulating our body to produce a lot of antibodies, but in the blood.
sentences.zh: 从那里，疫苗在刺激我们身体产生大量抗体方面做得非常好，但主要是在血液中。

sentences.en: And not a lot of those antibodies are going to make their way into the nose, which when you think about it, is really the place where the virus comes into the body.
sentences.zh: 而这些抗体中并没有多少能进入鼻腔，而当你思考一下，这实际上正是病毒进入人体的部位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This was always the case.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直如此。

sentences.en: This was the case even for the original virus.
sentences.zh: 即使对于原始病毒也是如此。

sentences.en: But with the original virus, just a small amount of antibodies was probably enough to stop the virus from multiplying in the nose.
sentences.zh: 但对于原始病毒，少量的抗体可能就足以阻止病毒在鼻腔中繁殖。

sentences.en: With Delta, there's just way too much virus for the small amount of antibodies in the nose to probably completely contain.
sentences.zh: 而对于德尔塔变异株，鼻腔中少量的抗体可能无法完全遏制住过多的病毒。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what you're describing, these breakthrough infections that are leaving vaccinated people with large viral loads that may make them spreaders,
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的这些突破性感染，让接种过疫苗的人体内携带大量病毒，可能使他们成为传播者，

sentences.en: that doesn't have a lot to do with the strength or weakness of our vaccines or them potentially wearing off.
sentences.zh: 这与我们疫苗的强弱或其效力可能减弱并没有太大关系。

sentences.en: It has a lot to do with the strength of the Delta variant and how it operates in the body, in particular, in the nose.
sentences.zh: 这与德尔塔变异株的强度以及它在人体内，特别是鼻腔内的运作方式有很大关系。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But the chances that you'll get infected with Delta if you're vaccinated are still very, very low.
sentences.zh: 但如果你接种了疫苗，感染德尔塔变异株的几率仍然非常非常低。

sentences.en: It's just once you do get infected, you do end up having a lot of virus.
sentences.zh: 只是当你一旦被感染，体内确实会携带大量病毒。

sentences.en: You keep referring to these breakthrough infections as rare.
sentences.zh: 你一直称这些突破性感染为罕见。

sentences.en: The chances is low.
sentences.zh: 几率很低。

sentences.en: Just how rare and just how low are the chances?
sentences.zh: 到底有多罕见，几率到底有多低？

sentences.en: Because in our last conversation, you described some pretty meaningfully large clusters.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们上次谈话中，你描述了一些相当大的聚集性病例。

sentences.en: And I get the sense that these breakthroughs may be somewhat widespread.
sentences.zh: 我感觉这些突破性感染可能相当普遍。

sentences.en: The short answer to your question is we don't really know yet how exactly rare they are.
sentences.zh: 对你问题的简短回答是，我们目前还不真正知道它们到底有多罕见。

sentences.en: There are some state-level data, and the Kaiser Family Foundation just looked at all of those data and said,
sentences.zh: 有一些州级数据，凯撒家庭基金会刚刚查看了所有这些数据并表示，

sentences.en: it looks like less than 1% of vaccinated people may end up with a breakthrough infection.
sentences.zh: 看起来不到1%的接种疫苗者可能会发生突破性感染。

sentences.en: They may have symptoms that are cold-like, that they may have a sore throat, they may cough, they may feel tired and have to take a couple of days off work at the most,
sentences.zh: 他们可能会出现类似感冒的症状，比如喉咙痛、咳嗽、感到疲倦，最多请几天假，

sentences.en: but they're not going to end up in the hospital, most likely.
sentences.zh: 但他们很可能不会最终住进医院。

sentences.en: And it's very, very unlikely that they would die.
sentences.zh: 而且他们死亡的可能性非常非常小。

sentences.en: But when you are vaccinated, it's supposed to be really difficult to get infected, and then really difficult, if you are infected, to have that much virus in your nose.
sentences.zh: 但是当你接种了疫苗，本应很难被感染，而且即使被感染，鼻腔里也很难有那么多的病毒。

sentences.en: So all of those things are happening now, and that is why the CDC changed its decision last week on whether vaccinated people should wear masks indoors in certain places.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些情况现在都在发生，这就是为什么美国疾控中心上周改变了关于接种疫苗者是否应该在某些室内场所佩戴口罩的决定。

sentences.en: Walk us through that new mask guidance and explain how it's connected to this new information about the breakthrough infections and the viral load.
sentences.zh: 请为我们梳理一下那项新的口罩指南，并解释它与关于突破性感染和病毒载量的新信息有何关联。

sentences.en: The CDC is saying that because vaccinated people can spread the virus to others,
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心表示，因为接种过疫苗的人可以将病毒传播给他人，

sentences.en: they should be wearing masks indoors, in public indoor spaces, especially in communities with high transmission.
sentences.zh: 他们应该在室内，在公共室内空间佩戴口罩，特别是在病毒传播率高的社区。

sentences.en: So when we look at the maps of the U.S., for example, the Times has them, and we see those large concentrations of red in Wyoming, Florida, parts of Missouri,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们查看美国地图时，例如《纽约时报》绘制的地图，我们看到怀俄明州、佛罗里达州、密苏里州部分地区有大片的红色区域，

sentences.en: those are high transmission areas.
sentences.zh: 那些就是高传播地区。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you could have a very low transmission state, because the state overall has, let's say, a fairly high vaccination rate, and they're not seeing very many cases.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一个传播率非常低的州，因为该州整体的疫苗接种率相当高，病例数也不多。

sentences.en: But there could be a few counties within that state that are red, where the virus is really finding a foothold.
sentences.zh: 但该州内可能仍有几个县是红色的，病毒在那里确实找到了立足点。

sentences.en: And people in those areas should be wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 而这些地区的人们应该佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: But everything you just told us is that theoretically, although it's rare,
sentences.zh: 但你刚才告诉我们的一切是，从理论上讲，虽然罕见，

sentences.en: any vaccinated person could be at risk of a breakthrough infection.
sentences.zh: 任何接种过疫苗的人都可能面临突破性感染的风险。

sentences.en: So why isn't this new mask guidance in place everywhere, given what we know about how transmissible Delta is and how quickly someone who has it can get on a plane
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于我们了解德尔塔变异株的传播性，以及携带者能多快登上飞机，

sentences.en: and go from a high transmission area to a low transmission area?
sentences.zh: 并从高传播地区前往低传播地区，为什么这项新的口罩指南没有在各地实施？

sentences.en: Isn't every part of the country potentially on the verge as a result of becoming a high transmission area?
sentences.zh: 难道全国的每一个地方不都可能因此处于成为高传播地区的边缘吗？

sentences.en: This is a really excellent question, and I think one that a lot of experts are asking as well, because why not make it universal masking at this point?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题，我想很多专家也在问，因为为什么此时不实行普遍佩戴口罩呢？

sentences.en: If there are counties that aren't quite at high transmission, they probably will be soon.
sentences.zh: 如果有些县还没有达到高传播水平，它们可能很快就会达到。

sentences.en: And there are many that are just on the cusp.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多县正处于临界点。

sentences.en: I think the CDC is trying to tread carefully, but I was able to look at a document last week that was shared internally within the CDC, and that one is not nearly as conservative.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国疾控中心正试图谨慎行事，但我上周看到了一份在美国疾控中心内部共享的文件，那份文件远没有那么保守。

sentences.en: In that document, CDC scientists were quite openly saying that the country should have universal masking.
sentences.zh: 在那份文件中，疾控中心的科学家们相当公开地表示，全国应该实行普遍佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So why isn't there going to be universal masking?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么不会实行普遍佩戴口罩呢？

sentences.en: It's a good question, and one I've asked the CDC.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题，我也问过美国疾控中心。

sentences.en: I'll let you know when I have an answer.
sentences.zh: 等我有答案了会告诉你。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So it seems like the CDC does not want to scare people, wants to take a narrow, judicious, modest approach to what it has just learned.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来美国疾控中心不想吓唬民众，想对其刚刚了解到的情况采取一种狭隘、审慎、温和的态度。

sentences.en: I think that's understandable for a public health agency.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于一个公共卫生机构来说，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: I mean, the CDC's job is to lead people and give them guidance, but to do so in a way that doesn't cause people to panic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，疾控中心的工作是引导民众并提供指导，但要以一种不会引起恐慌的方式进行。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But there was this document, the internal CDC document, and that described the Delta variant as more contagious than SARS and MERS, you know, the previous coronaviruses,
sentences.zh: 但有那份文件，那份内部的疾控中心文件，它将德尔塔变异株描述为比非典（SARS）和中东呼吸综合征（MERS）——你知道，之前的冠状病毒——更具传染性，

sentences.en: more contagious than the common cold, more contagious than the flu, than the 1918 flu, than Ebola.
sentences.zh: 比普通感冒更具传染性，比流感、1918年大流感、埃博拉病毒更具传染性。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: One of the things it said that really made me set up and take notice is it said the next step for the CDC is to acknowledge that the war has changed.
sentences.zh: 它提到的让我真正坐直并引起注意的一点是，它说美国疾控中心的下一步是承认这场战争已经改变了。

sentences.en: Meaning the war on COVID.
sentences.zh: 意思是针对新冠病毒的战争。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And I think that's because the enemy has changed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为敌人已经改变了。

sentences.en: Delta is not anything like the original enemy that we were fighting.
sentences.zh: 德尔塔变异株与我们最初抗击的敌人完全不同。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《纽约时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《纽约时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Apoorva, let's talk through the practical implications of this new information we're getting and how people are starting to act on it or should act on it.
sentences.zh: 那么阿普尔瓦，让我们谈谈我们获得的新信息在实际层面的影响，以及人们开始如何应对或应该如何应对。

sentences.en: What are we seeing?
sentences.zh: 我们看到了什么？

sentences.en: It's only been a few days and I think things are going to change a lot in the coming days, but already we're seeing some reactions.
sentences.zh: 才过了几天，我认为未来几天情况会有很大变化，但我们已经看到了一些反应。

sentences.en: Disney and Walmart, the latest companies announcing vaccine mandates for employees.
sentences.zh: 迪士尼和沃尔玛是最新宣布对员工实施疫苗强制令的公司。

sentences.en: It follows Uber, Jefferies, Facebook, Google, Netflix and the federal government.
sentences.zh: 此前优步、杰富瑞、脸书、谷歌、奈飞和联邦政府也采取了类似措施。

sentences.en: You know, we've had companies put in vaccine mandates for all their employees and some companies have decided not to bring their employees back to the office.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们已经有公司对所有员工实施了疫苗强制令，一些公司决定不让员工回到办公室。

sentences.en: Companies like Lyft are delaying six months to February.
sentences.zh: 像 Lyft 这样的公司将返岗时间推迟了六个月，延至明年二月。

sentences.en: Apple and Google also pushing back their dates and Twitter closed its offices in New York and San Francisco due to the surge in cases.
sentences.zh: 苹果和谷歌也推迟了他们的日期，推特则因病例激增关闭了其在纽约和旧金山的办公室。

sentences.en: Some places put in masking mandates.
sentences.zh: 一些地方实施了口罩强制令。

sentences.en: The CDC's new mask guidance has triggered mask mandates in New Orleans, Washington, D.C., even Broadway theaters.
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心新的口罩指南已经在新奥尔良、华盛顿特区，甚至百老汇剧院引发了口罩强制令。

sentences.en: And it's now under consideration in San Francisco and New York.
sentences.zh: 目前旧金山和纽约也在考虑之中。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of change and I think we'll see a lot more of it and it'll be very patchy like everything else in this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以变化很大，我认为我们会看到更多变化，而且会像这场疫情中的其他一切一样，非常不均衡。

sentences.en: I think some will react by putting in a lot of precautions into place and some will do nothing.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些人会通过采取大量预防措施来应对，而有些人则什么都不做。

sentences.en: I want to zero in on one of the things that you mentioned, which is companies delaying their return to office.
sentences.zh: 我想重点谈谈你提到的其中一件事，即公司推迟员工返岗。

sentences.en: As it happens, that's something that's impacting us very intimately because our employer, The Times, just announced that we won't be returned to office
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，这件事对我们影响非常直接，因为我们的雇主《纽约时报》刚刚宣布，我们不会在九月份返岗，

sentences.en: in September because of this new information.
sentences.zh: 因为这些新信息。

sentences.en: They're going to delay that indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 他们将无限期推迟返岗。

sentences.en: But why do you think companies are delaying the return of workers to the office?
sentences.zh: 但你认为公司为什么要推迟员工返岗？

sentences.en: Wouldn't a vaccine mandate solve that problem?
sentences.zh: 强制疫苗接种难道不能解决这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Because then the risk of transmission would still be relatively low despite breakthrough infections happening.
sentences.zh: 因为即便发生了突破性感染，传播风险依然相对较低。

sentences.en: A lot of companies haven't really put vaccine mandates into place because it's very complicated.
sentences.zh: 很多公司并没有真正实施强制疫苗接种，因为这非常复杂。

sentences.en: But even if companies do put one in place, I think what this data is telling us is it's very rare for somebody who's vaccinated to get a breakthrough infection,
sentences.zh: 但即便公司实施了强制接种，我认为这些数据告诉我们，已接种疫苗的人出现突破性感染的情况非常罕见，

sentences.en: but it does happen, right?
sentences.zh: 但这种情况确实会发生，对吧？

sentences.en: And if you are somebody who's vaccinated and has someone at home who's immunocompromised or who has kids who haven't been vaccinated yet, even if it's a small risk,
sentences.zh: 如果你已经接种了疫苗，但家里有免疫功能低下的人，或者有还没接种疫苗的孩子，即使风险很小，

sentences.en: you may not want to take that risk and go into an office and be around people who may bring the virus to you and then you bring that home.
sentences.zh: 你可能也不想冒这个险去办公室，接触那些可能把病毒带给你，然后你再把病毒带回家的人。

sentences.en: So the thinking is it's just not worth taking the risk.
sentences.zh: 所以大家的想法是，这不值得冒险。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为是对的。

sentences.en: And maybe all of these companies will be able to revisit that decision sometime this fall if Delta comes back down like it did in the UK and like it did in India,
sentences.zh: 也许今年秋天，如果德尔塔毒株像在英国和印度那样回落，所有这些公司都能重新考虑这个决定，

sentences.en: but it's just too soon to tell.
sentences.zh: 但现在下结论还为时过早。

sentences.en: You mentioned kids, Apoor, but this new information and this new guidance from the CDC would seem to have pretty meaningful implications for education.
sentences.zh: Apoorva，你提到了孩子，但CDC的这些新信息和新指南似乎对教育领域有着相当重大的影响。

sentences.en: It does, because the CDC said that there should be universal masking in schools across the country, not just in places with high transmission, but everywhere.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，因为CDC表示全国各地的学校都应该全面佩戴口罩，不仅仅是在高传播地区，而是所有地方。

sentences.en: And that means that every kid over two should probably be wearing a mask, all teachers, all staff should be wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 这意味着每个两岁以上的孩子可能都应该戴口罩，所有的老师和员工也都应该戴口罩。

sentences.en: And that's going to go down okay in some places and not at all in others.
sentences.zh: 这在某些地方会顺利推行，但在其他地方则完全行不通。

sentences.en: But I think the CDC made that decision because we know now how important it is to have kids back in school and it's worth doing whatever we can
sentences.zh: 但我认为CDC做出这个决定是因为我们现在知道让孩子重返校园有多重要，无论我们能做什么都是值得的，

sentences.en: to make sure that they still have a place to go and learn every day.
sentences.zh: 以确保他们每天仍然有一个可以去学习的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Returning to the office in some people's minds might not be worth it, but in the minds of people at the CDC, returning to school is very much worth it.
sentences.zh: 在一些人看来，重返办公室可能不值得，但在CDC看来，重返校园是非常值得的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So beyond the workplace and beyond schools, let's turn to what this means for our day-to-day interactions.
sentences.zh: 那么，除了工作场所和学校，让我们谈谈这对我们日常互动意味着什么。

sentences.en: And we've done this with you in the past, Apoorva.
sentences.zh: Apoorva，我们过去也和你讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you some scenarios and have you help us think through the best way for us to approach them.
sentences.zh: 我会给你一些场景，请你帮我们思考一下应对它们的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Let's take the example of two vaccinated friends.
sentences.zh: 让我们以两个已接种疫苗的朋友为例。

sentences.en: Very grateful that over the past couple of months, they've been encouraged to spend time together indoors, have drinks, no masks, have dinner.
sentences.zh: 非常庆幸的是，在过去的几个月里，他们被鼓励在室内共度时光、喝酒、不戴口罩、共进晚餐。

sentences.en: Now, we're being told that one of them could theoretically have a breakthrough infection of COVID and a high viral load and pass it on to the other person
sentences.zh: 现在，我们被告知其中一人理论上可能会发生新冠突破性感染，且病毒载量很高，并将其传染给另一个人，

sentences.en: who could then pass it on to their family.
sentences.zh: 而那个人随后可能会将其传染给他们的家人。

sentences.en: Should we now think of our vaccinated friends as potential risks?
sentences.zh: 我们现在应该把已接种疫苗的朋友视为潜在的风险来源吗？

sentences.en: A lot of this depends on what your personal tolerance for risk is.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于你个人的风险承受能力。

sentences.en: If you live in an area with low transmission of virus and you don't live with anybody who's immunocompromised and you don't have kids under 12
sentences.zh: 如果你住在一个病毒传播率低的地区，家里没有免疫功能低下的人，也没有12岁以下的孩子，

sentences.en: and you don't think you'll be interacting with anybody who is at risk and you don't mind yourself getting mild symptoms, then yes, of course,
sentences.zh: 而且你认为自己不会接触到任何高危人群，也不介意自己出现轻微症状，那么是的，当然，

sentences.en: you can have dinner with a friend indoors.
sentences.zh: 你可以和朋友在室内共进晚餐。

sentences.en: But if you do live with anybody who is vulnerable or may come into contact with someone who is, then I think we're going back a few months
sentences.zh: 但如果你确实和任何脆弱人群住在一起，或者可能会接触到这样的人，那么我认为我们又回到了几个月前，

sentences.en: to where we were socializing mostly outdoors and wearing masks whenever we saw people indoors.
sentences.zh: 那时我们主要在户外社交，在室内见到人时都会戴上口罩。

sentences.en: And if you live in a high transmission area, you should be wearing a mask in all public indoor spaces.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在高传播地区，在所有公共室内场所都应该戴口罩。

sentences.en: That's what the CDC guidance is telling us.
sentences.zh: 这就是CDC指南告诉我们的。

sentences.en: So according to that thinking, even vaccinated parents with kids under 12 should probably be masked when socializing indoors because they could spread the virus,
sentences.zh: 所以按照这种思路，即使是已接种疫苗且有12岁以下孩子的父母，在室内社交时也应该戴口罩，因为他们可能会传播病毒，

sentences.en: a breakthrough, a case of the virus, to their unvaccinated children.
sentences.zh: 即突破性感染病例，传染给他们未接种疫苗的孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as we know, kids are at very low risk of getting infected.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，孩子感染的风险非常低。

sentences.en: And even when they do, they have very mild symptoms and they don't really transmit to others very efficiently.
sentences.zh: 即使他们感染了，症状也非常轻微，而且他们传播给别人的效率并不高。

sentences.en: But the risk is not zero.
sentences.zh: 但风险并非为零。

sentences.en: So a lot depends on your kid's health and how many risks you want to take with it.
sentences.zh: 所以这在很大程度上取决于你孩子的健康状况，以及你想为此承担多少风险。

sentences.en: It feels like we lost something kind of important this week.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们这周失去了一些相当重要的东西。

sentences.en: And it may be mostly psychological, but meaningful, which is the idea that the vaccine meant that most people were not going to spread the virus,
sentences.zh: 这可能主要是心理上的，但意义重大，那就是疫苗意味着大多数人不会传播病毒，

sentences.en: that we, those of us who got the vaccine,
sentences.zh: 我们这些接种了疫苗的人，

sentences.en: were going to be part of the solution, which is not just keeping ourselves safe, but contributing to the end of this global scourge because we could not become vectors ourselves.
sentences.zh: 将成为解决方案的一部分，这不仅是为了保护我们自己，也是为了终结这场全球灾难，因为我们自己不会成为病毒的载体。

sentences.en: And now we don't have that same assurance anymore.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们不再有那种保证了。

sentences.en: And that feels like a pretty big loss.
sentences.zh: 这感觉是一个相当大的损失。

sentences.en: I think it's a loss if you look at it in a glass-half-empty way.
sentences.zh: 如果你以悲观的角度来看，我认为这是一种损失。

sentences.en: I think the glass-half-full view is you may get a little bit infected, you may pass it to somebody else, but you are still doing a great service by not getting sick,
sentences.zh: 我认为乐观的角度是，你可能会轻微感染，可能会传染给别人，但你通过不生病，仍然做出了巨大的贡献，

sentences.en: by not burdening the healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 没有给医疗系统增加负担。

sentences.en: And I really don't want to forget here that we've said the breakthrough infections are rare.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想忘记我们之前说过突破性感染是罕见的。

sentences.en: It's not like all of us are going to go out and spread the virus.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们所有人都会出去传播病毒。

sentences.en: So I think there is a way to look at this that is not bleak.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有一种看待这个问题的方式并不悲观。

sentences.en: So are we maybe missing the bigger picture here if we focus on vaccinated people and breakthrough infections and viral load, which is that this really is still a pandemic
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们关注已接种疫苗的人、突破性感染和病毒载量，是否忽略了更大的图景，即这仍然是一场未接种疫苗者的疫情，

sentences.en: of the unvaccinated, despite this new information?
sentences.zh: 尽管有了这些新信息？

sentences.en: I'm so glad you asked me that.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你问我这个问题。

sentences.en: We can't take our eye off the ball, which is we need to vaccinate as many people in this country as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 我们不能转移注意力，重点仍然是我们需要尽快为国内尽可能多的人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: As long as we have this massive number of people who are unvaccinated, who can keep getting infected and spreading the virus, we're going to see these waves and surges
sentences.zh: 只要我们还有如此庞大数量的人未接种疫苗，他们就会不断被感染并传播病毒，我们就会看到这些浪潮和激增，

sentences.en: and we'll need to take precautions.
sentences.zh: 我们需要采取预防措施。

sentences.en: I know that we've spent all this time talking about breakthrough infections and vaccinated people and that they can spread the virus, but the vaccines are doing their job.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们花了很多时间讨论突破性感染、已接种疫苗的人以及他们可以传播病毒，但疫苗正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: They were designed to stop people from getting really sick, ending up in the hospital and dying.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计初衷是阻止人们患重病、住院和死亡。

sentences.en: And they are doing that very well.
sentences.zh: 而且它们做得非常好。

sentences.en: Really, the only way that we can get out of this pandemic is to vaccinate as many people as possible.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们摆脱这场疫情的唯一途径就是为尽可能多的人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Well, Apoorva, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，Apoorva，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Michael。

sentences.en: And I hope not to have to talk to you really soon.
sentences.zh: 我希望很快不用再和你交谈。

sentences.en: But just in case, we'll put you down for next Monday.
sentences.zh: 但以防万一，我们把你排在下周一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: In an interview on Sunday, the head of the National Institutes of Health,
sentences.zh: 在周日的一次采访中，美国国立卫生研究院院长，

sentences.en: Francis Collins,
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·柯林斯，

sentences.en: praised government agencies and private companies who are now requiring that their workers be vaccinated and encouraged employers across the country to do the same.
sentences.zh: 赞扬了现在要求员工接种疫苗的政府机构和私营公司，并鼓励全国各地的雇主也这样做。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to see employers like Disney and Walmart coming out and asking their staff now to be vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到像迪士尼和沃尔玛这样的雇主站出来，要求他们的员工现在接种疫苗。

sentences.en: I'm glad to see the president has said all federal employees I oversee NIH with 45,000 people need to also get vaccinated or if they're not, to get regular testing,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到总统表示，我所监管的拥有45000名员工的NIH的所有联邦雇员也需要接种疫苗，如果不接种，则需要定期进行检测，

sentences.en: which is inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 这很不方便。

sentences.en: All of those steps, I think, are in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些步骤都是朝着正确的方向迈进。

sentences.en: But I think maybe that's what it will take for some of those who've still been a little reluctant to say, OK, it's time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，对于那些仍然有些犹豫的人来说，这可能就是让他们说“好吧，是时候了”所需要的动力。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: In the latest example of a cluster of breakthrough infections, at least 233 workers at two major hospitals in San Francisco, most of them vaccinated,
sentences.zh: 在最近发生的一起突破性感染群聚案例中，旧金山两家大型医院的至少233名员工，其中大多数已接种疫苗，

sentences.en: have tested positive for COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 新冠病毒检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: The majority of the workers were infected with the Delta variant and a nationwide moratorium on residential evictions put in place by the CDC last fall has expired over the weekend
sentences.zh: 大多数员工感染的是德尔塔变异株，而CDC去年秋天实施的全国住宅驱逐禁令已于周末到期，

sentences.en: after efforts by the Biden administration to win an extension had failed.
sentences.zh: 此前拜登政府争取延期的努力均告失败。

sentences.en: The expiration puts hundreds of thousands of tenants at risk of losing their shelter just as COVID-19 infections surge across the country.
sentences.zh: 随着新冠病毒感染在全国范围内激增，这一禁令的到期使数十万租户面临失去住所的风险。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Jessica Chung,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Rob Zipko、Jessica Chung、

sentences.en: Diana Nguyen, and Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: Diana Nguyen和Alexandra Lee Young制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett and Lisa Chow and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由Paige Cowett和Lisa Chow剪辑，Chris Wood负责工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备节假日待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: The Wirecutter Show
sentences.zh: 《Wirecutter秀》
